parsed.explanation: The combined regime stacks a universal entry exposure on top of a live criminal offence against gender presentation. Airport screening compares appearance to passport sex, with documented hours-long detentions, genital X-rays, mockery, passport confiscation and refusal spanning 2016–2025 and transit denial in 2025. Gender nonconformity is itself criminal: a foreign trans woman was sentenced to one year and a fine in 2017, held nearly three weeks in a cell for effeminate detainees, head shaved and hormones destroyed, then deported — the broad presentation offence remains replaced but in force. Custody torture is documented, a trans visitor has been held since September 2022 with no sourced release, and no discrimination law, NGO, or remedy exists. No credible execution pathway is documented.

entry_documents.exposure: Universal screening compares appearance with passport sex at the two main gateways: 2025 detentions with genital X-rays, mockery, refusal and passport confiscation; 2022 nine-hour interrogation and deportation; 2016 five-hour detention; May 2025 transit refusal. Refusals documented across a decade.
entry_documents.protection: None documented. Record does not state whether a consistent gender marker changes the outcome.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry refusal flows to deportation and passport seizure; transit denial strands the traveller mid-journey regardless of onward ticket.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: 2017 visitor arrested in a mall in jeans and sentenced to one year plus 10,000 fine without counsel; ~3 weeks in a cell for effeminate detainees, head shaved, hormones discarded. Beatings and forced rectal examinations documented as torture in custody. A trans visitor held since September 2022; release not sourced.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Sentence converted to deportation; one 2017 tourist's unrelated indecency charge was dropped after head-of-government intervention — discretionary, not trans-specific.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Presentation arrest → custodial placement with other gender-nonconforming detainees → medication loss → deportation.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal presentation offence uniform across emirates, layered in 2017 with a local public-morals offence; local campaigns and a venue shutdown documented in the other gateway city.
federal_state_facilities.protection: None documented. No emirate is recorded as more permissive.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Emirate-level charges can be added to the federal offence, increasing exposure without providing relief.

care_services.exposure: Hormones destroyed in custody; state-restricted surgery; conversion practices not prohibited; involuntary hormonal treatment documented in same-sex-conduct cases; no anti-discrimination law covering care.
care_services.interaction: Detention directly causes care interruption; emergency disclosure of trans status feeds the presentation offence.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Article 412(2) (in force January 2022) penalises cross-dressing into women-only spaces by up to one year and 10,000 dirhams, but enforcement targets appearance in ordinary mixed-gender places. Officials declare no room for queer acts; trans-flag and LGBTQ content censored.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Same-sex conduct offence is complaint-based with no eligible complainant between adult men, and no consensual-conduct prosecutions documented since 2015 — a narrow, secondary mitigant.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Presentation charge proceeds state-initiated, independent of any complainant, and typically ends in deportation.

minors_guardians.exposure: Not documented. A child accompanying a parent refused entry or held overnight would plausibly face separation, but no sourced case exists.
minors_guardians.interaction: Uncertain: entry refusal or detention of a guardian would orphan the itinerary, but the record is silent.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Police as perpetrators: 2011 campaign targeting transsexuals and masculine-presenting women; 2013 visitors detained for calling police; 2017 mall arrests; 2020 clothing arrests of foreign residents. No organisation exists to report to; the community night was shut down.
street_violence_police_response.protection: None documented for trans people; police hostilities are the recorded pattern rather than protection.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Seeking police help can invert into arrest, as the 2013 nightclub complainants show.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination law, no legal gender recognition, LGBTI organisations cannot register, no open NGO anywhere; 2017 sentence imposed without representation; 2022 custody outcome unresolved; no aggregate refusal figures.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Not documented. No effective visitor-facing remedy appears in the record.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Absence of civil society removes the intermediary that converts an airport or street incident into a challenge.

anchor_checks.comparison: Same tier. Varnalia criminalises presentation, arrests at transit checks, holds people for long periods with beatings and illusory remedies and has an unapplied capital clause. This dossier matches: a visitor actually imprisoned, custody abuse, torture documented, no remedy. Ours lacks any credible capital provision, but adds a decade-long universal airport anatomy-screening exposure Varnalia does not describe.

Higher than this case, so ours sits below it. Varnalia-2 has weekly raids, fines, detention and 'imprisonment rare'; appeals exist though slow. Here imprisonment was imposed on a foreign visitor, entry screening is continuous and unavoidable, and no organisation or appeal route is documented — two heavier features than the 0.25 anchor carries.

Materially above this case. Vellandra excludes and humiliates but explicitly 'without arrest or criminal charge', and appeals exist however ineffective. Here a criminal offence with a one-year sentence has been applied to a visitor, custody conditions are abusive, and torture in custody is documented — severity far beyond exclusion.

parsed.synthesis: The two gateway airports create an inescapable discovery mechanism: every trans traveller's presentation is measured against passport sex, with anatomy checks, hours of detention, confiscation and refusal documented as recently as 2025. Discovery then feeds a criminal regime that has actually imprisoned and deported a foreign visitor for wearing jeans, in a system with no anti-discrimination law, no registered organisation, censored support channels, and documented custodial abuse including torture and hormone destruction. The complaint-based same-sex statute and its non-enforcement since 2015 are genuine but tangential; they do not touch the state-initiated presentation charge. A traveller with a minor compounds separation risk, though that is undocumented. No credible execution pathway exists, keeping this above the extreme floor but firmly in severe-risk territory.
